metadata.title: Leverandørvakt – early warnings about your suppliers
metadata.description: Follow your suppliers and customers and get notified when something changes for the worse: new roles, annual accounts, bankruptcy and risk signals, from open data in the Brønnøysund Register Centre.

header.colorScheme: Switch between light and dark mode

hero.title: Know when a supplier changes for the worse, before it costs you
hero.lead: Follow your suppliers and customers. Leverandørvakt checks the Brønnøysund registers around the clock and tells you when a CEO leaves, an auditor resigns, accounts are late or a company goes bankrupt.

accounts.text: Equity turned negative in the 2025 accounts

features.title: What Leverandørvakt watches for you
features.lead: Everything is based on official, open data. Every warning says what changed, when and why it matters.

changes.title: Changes in the register
changes.text: New CEO, board or auditor, a new address, bankruptcy or liquidation. Brønnøysund's update feeds are checked every ten minutes.

accounts.title: Annual accounts
accounts.text: New and corrected filings, equity turning negative and audits being dropped, compared year by year.

risk.title: Risk signals you can explain
risk.text: A check before you sign: every signal with its weight and reason, and what could not be checked. Support for your own assessment, not a credit rating.

connections.title: Connections
connections.text: See when the same people or audit firm hold roles across your suppliers and customers, or in a company you are considering.

trends.title: Regional trends
trends.text: New companies per month by municipality and industry, compared with the same period a year earlier.

assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.text: Ask in plain language, in English or Norwegian: “Which of my suppliers have the highest risk?” It only reads your data, it never changes it.

about.title: About Leverandørvakt
about.lead: Leverandørvakt keeps an eye on the Norwegian companies you depend on, and tells you when one of them changes for the worse.

why.title: Why it exists
why.text1: Small and medium-sized businesses rarely notice that a supplier or customer is in trouble until an invoice goes unpaid or a delivery does not arrive. The signs are often public long before that: a CEO leaves, the auditor resigns, the annual accounts are late, or equity turns negative.
why.text2: All of this is registered with the Brønnøysund Register Centre, but nobody has time to check every partner by hand. Leverandørvakt does it for you, every ten minutes, and only tells you about what matters.

roles.title: Roles.
roles.text: New CEO, chair, board members, auditor or accountant.

status.title: Status.
status.text: Bankruptcy, liquidation, forced liquidation, or being struck off the register.

accounts.title: Annual accounts.
accounts.text: New and corrected filings, equity turning negative, audits being dropped, and accounts that are overdue after 31 July.

risk.title: Risk signals.
risk.text: An assessment that shows every signal, its weight and its reason, and what could not be checked.

connections.title: Connections.
connections.text: People or audit firms that hold roles in several of your companies.

data.title: Where the data comes from
data.text: Everything is open data from Norwegian public agencies. Nothing is bought, scraped or guessed.
data.brreg: the Central Coordinating Register for Legal Entities, roles, update feeds and the Register of Company Accounts
data.ssb: industry names from the Standard Industrial Classification

risk.title: What the risk assessment is, and is not
risk.text1: The risk level is calculated from public register data with fixed, documented rules: each warning sign adds points, and some signs, like bankruptcy, give high risk on their own. Every assessment shows its reasons.
risk.limits: It is support for your own assessment, not a credit rating. It does not know about unpaid invoices, court cases or anything else outside the public registers, and changes are only known from the day someone started following a company.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.account: Your account holds your name, email address and a securely hashed password.
privacy.watchlist: Your watchlist and notes are only visible to you. The notes are never sent to the AI assistant.
privacy.notifications: Notifications are kept so you can read them later.
privacy.notStored: Birth dates of the people behind a company are used to tell people with the same name apart, but they are never stored or shown.

project.title: About this project
project.text: Leverandørvakt is an independent portfolio project built by a full-stack developer in Norway.
project.byName: Leverandørvakt is an independent portfolio project built by {name}, a full-stack developer in Norway.
project.built: The API is written in Node.js and TypeScript with Express and PostgreSQL, and is covered by more than 300 automated tests that run on every change. The web app uses Next.js and Designsystemet, the design system of the Norwegian public sector.
project.independent: It is not affiliated with the Brønnøysund Register Centre or any other agency, and it is not a commercial service.

guide.title: Guide
guide.lead: How to follow your suppliers and customers with Leverandørvakt, what is watched, and what you see when something happens.

start.title: Getting started
start.text: Create an account, then follow the companies you depend on. Everything else builds on your watchlist.

search.title: Search.
search.text: Find a company by name, or type its nine-digit organization number to go straight to it.

follow.title: Follow.
follow.text: Press Follow on the company page. From then on, changes are recorded and you are notified.

note.title: Write a note.
note.text: A private note reminds you why you follow the company. Only you can see it, and it is never sent to the assistant's language model.

watched.title: What is watched
watched.text: Leverandørvakt reads the Brønnøysund Register Centre's update feeds every ten minutes and compares each followed company with what was stored last time. Annual accounts are checked once a day.

status.title: Status:
status.text: bankruptcy, being wound up, forced liquidation and being struck off the register.

roles.title: Roles:
roles.text: the CEO, the chair and other board members, the auditor and the accountant.

details.title: Company details:
details.text: name, organization form, business address, website, industry and number of employees.

accounts.title: Annual accounts:
accounts.text: new filings, corrected filings and key figures such as revenue, result and equity.

risk.title: Reading the risk level
risk.text: Each company gets a risk level built from warning signs in the public registers. The risk tab shows exactly which signs were found and why.

level.title: Low, medium or high.
level.text: A critical sign, such as bankruptcy, always gives high risk. Otherwise the level follows the score.

score.title: Score from 0 to 100.
score.text: Each warning sign adds points: 20 or more is medium, 40 or more is high.

signals.title: Warning signs,
signals.text: such as negative equity, a loss, missing accounts after the 31 July deadline or frequent changes of CEO or address.

limits.title: What could not be checked,
limits.text: such as a company too new to have filed accounts. A short list of signs is not the same as a clean bill of health.

risk.notCredit: The risk level is based only on public register data. It is not a credit rating, and it does not replace your own judgement or a credit check.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.text: When a followed company changes, you get a notification. The bell in the header shows the unread count and the latest ones; the Notifications page shows them all, with the value before and after the change. Each has a severity:

critical.title: Critical:
critical.text: the company may no longer be able to deliver or pay: bankruptcy, being wound up or forced liquidation.

warning.title: Warning:
warning.text: worth a closer look, such as a new CEO, chair or auditor, a new name or address, or negative equity.

info.title: Info:
info.text: for the record, such as new board members, a new website or newly filed accounts.

accounts.title: Annual accounts
accounts.text: The accounts tab shows revenue, net result and equity per year as a chart and as a table. Losses are drawn below the zero line. Companies must send their accounts by 31 July the year after; a missing filing after that date is a warning sign.

trends.title: Trends
trends.text: The Trends page shows how many companies are registered per month compared with a year earlier, and the most common industries. Filter by municipality, main industry, organization form and period to see what is happening where you do business.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.text: Ask about your companies in plain language, in English or Norwegian. The assistant looks things up in your watchlist, the registers and the trends, and answers with what it found.

ask.title: Good questions
ask.text: are about your own companies: “Which have the highest risk, and why?”, “What changed this week?” or “Do any share a board member?”

sources.title: Under each answer
sources.text: you see what it is based on, such as the risk assessment or the annual accounts.

private.title: It only reads.
private.text: It cannot follow, unfollow or change anything, and your private notes are never sent to the model.

limit.title: There is a daily limit
limit.text: of questions per user, counted over the last 24 hours. The number left is shown under the question box.

scenarios.title: Scenarios
scenarios.text: What you see in Leverandørvakt when something happens to a company you follow.

bankrupt.title: A supplier goes bankrupt
bankrupt.happens: The court opens bankruptcy proceedings, and the register marks the company as bankrupt.
bankrupt.see: A critical notification within about ten minutes, a Bankrupt tag on the company, and the risk level goes to high.
bankrupt.do: Contact the estate about open orders and deliveries, and start looking for another supplier.

newCeo.title: A customer gets a new CEO and board
newCeo.happens: The roles are changed in the register.
newCeo.see: A warning for the new CEO and one for the new chair, an info notification for the other board members, each with the old and new people.
newCeo.do: Check the Roles tab, and ask the assistant whether the new people are also on the boards of your other companies.

lateAccounts.title: The accounts are late
lateAccounts.happens: 31 July passes without accounts for last year being filed.
lateAccounts.see: A warning sign on the risk tab saying which year is missing and when it was due, and a higher risk score.
lateAccounts.do: Ask the company why, and consider safer payment terms until the accounts are in.

newCustomer.title: Checking a new customer before you sign
newCustomer.happens: You are about to give a new customer credit.
newCustomer.see: Search for the company: the overview, roles, accounts and risk tabs show its status, key people, figures and warning signs, even before you follow it.
newCustomer.do: Follow it if you go ahead, so you are told if things change. You can stop following at any time.

more.title: Ready to start?
more.text: Follow your first company and the overview page will guide you through the rest.
